title: My ML model called the BTC drop. Approximately 9,650 points in profit.
author: Public_Luck_4753
selftext:
​

Hey guys,

Finally, a solid result to share!

The SHORT signal generated by my ML model on 10 November closed on 14 November at 23:59 UTC, capturing approximately **9,650 points**.

*Entry:* 73,800  

*Exit:* 64,150

I've attached the chart showing the complete move.

What makes this trade particularly satisfying is that the model identified the bearish direction ahead of the drop. After a few trades that didn't go as expected, it's good to see the system deliver a result like this.

For those who don't know, I've been developing this BTC prediction model for several years. It's a machine learning-based system that analyses market data and generates 5-day directional predictions with probability estimates, indicating the likelihood of BTC moving bullish or bearish.

Unlike conventional indicators based on fixed rules, the model is designed to adapt to changing market conditions by continuously learning from incoming market data.

I've spent years backtesting and developing it, followed by a year of live trading. I've also maintained MT5 trading records for the past four months, so there's a substantial amount of historical and live performance data behind the project.

Building something like this has been a long journey, and I'm genuinely interested in hearing what other people think about this approach to systematic BTC trading.

Would be interesting to hear your thoughts!

comments.author: DatGiantIsopod
comments.body:
Okay - but between 4th Oct and 10th Nov BTC dropped from 87k to 73k. Without meaning to sound critical, what exactly sets your model apart from a simple trend following model? Because the entire decline was around 29% (~87k - ~62k) peak to bottom, of which you captured roughly around 13% or just over a third. 

Honestly not meaning to sound critical since you seem stoked on the results, and your model captured the (recent) bottom fairly well, but just curious about how you're defining this as a "prediction model" that "identified the bearish direction ahead of the drop" when in actual fact the market had been in steady decline for a  over a month beforehand?
